Since \(8^2+15^2=17^2\), triangle \(ABC\) is right-angled at \(C\).

Its area is

\[
[ABC]=\frac12(8)(15)=60.
\]

Let \(CD\) be the altitude to hypotenuse \(AB\). Then

\[
[ABC]=\frac12(AB)(CD)=\frac12(17)(CD),
\]

so

\[
CD=\frac{120}{17}.
\]

In a right triangle, the projection of leg \(AC\) onto the hypotenuse satisfies

\[
AC^2=AD\cdot AB.
\]

Thus

\[
AD=\frac{AC^2}{AB}=\frac{8^2}{17}=\frac{64}{17}.
\]

Now triangle \(ACD\) is right-angled at \(D\), so

\[
[ACD]=\frac12(AD)(CD)
=\frac12\left(\frac{64}{17}\right)\left(\frac{120}{17}\right)
=\frac{3840}{289}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{3840}{289}}
\]
